title: Chase flatness theorem for torsionless modules over semihereditary rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that every finitely generated ideal is projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Suppose there are a set $A$ and an injective $R$-linear map $M\hookrightarrow\prod_{a\in A}R$, where the product consists of all functions $A\to R$ with componentwise module operations (this is the torsionless condition). Then $M$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma 6.10, proof, last sentence: a torsionless module over a semihereditary ring is flat by Chase; HRS cites Lam, Lectures on modules and rings (1999), Definition 4.64 and Theorem 4.67. No Stacks tag for this theorem is asserted.

proof.text: Write the given embedding as $e:M\hookrightarrow R^A$. Fix $n\ge0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in M$ with $\sum_i f_ix_i=0$. Set $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ and let $q:R^n\to I$ send $(r_i)$ to $\sum_i f_ir_i$. The map $q$ is surjective by the description of the generated ideal. By hypothesis $I$ is projective. Apply the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to $q$ and $\mathrm{id}_I$, obtaining $s:I\to R^n$ with $qs=\mathrm{id}_I$. Put $p=\mathrm{id}_{R^n}-sq$. Then $qp=0$, and $p(v)=v$ whenever $q(v)=0$, directly from these formulas.

source.place: Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), splitting a surjection onto a projective module; Tag 00HK (lemma-flat-eq), equational criterion. Agent-written matrix argument for the Chase assertion cited by HRS Lemma 6.10.

proof.text: Let $b_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector, and define $a_{ij}\in R$ by $p(b_j)=(a_{ij})_i$. Since $qp(b_j)=0$, we have $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$. For each $\alpha\in A$ put $v_\alpha=(e(x_i)(\alpha))_i$. Applying evaluation at $\alpha$ to the given relation yields $\sum_i f_i e(x_i)(\alpha)=0$, so $q(v_\alpha)=0$. Thus $v_\alpha=p(v_\alpha)=\sum_j e(x_j)(\alpha)p(b_j)$ by linearity and the coordinate-vector expansion. Its $i$th coordinate says $e(x_i)(\alpha)=\sum_j a_{ij}e(x_j)(\alpha)$. Therefore $e(x_i)=e(\sum_j a_{ij}x_j)$ as functions on $A$. Injectivity of $e$ gives $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}x_j$. This argument uses only finite sums, linearity and equality of functions.

source.place: Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), splitting a surjection onto a projective module; Tag 00HK (lemma-flat-eq), equational criterion. Agent-written matrix argument for the Chase assertion cited by HRS Lemma 6.10.

proof.text: Take $m=n$ and $y_j=x_j$. The two identities just established, $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$, say exactly that the arbitrary relation $\sum_i f_ix_i=0$ is trivial in the terminology of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion]. That node applies to any module over a commutative ring; it implies that $M$ is flat. The case $n=0$ uses the empty matrix and empty family and is included.
